eraCell.selected: node v8.11.4 (official darwin-x64 build), bundled npm 5.6.0
eraCell.policyForSelection: the application declares no engines range and carries no .nvmrc. The strongest era statement it makes about its own Node is its own Dockerfile: `ARG NODE_IMAGE=node:8.11`, and that image is the stage that runs `npm install` and `npm run build:prod`. The 8.11 line was therefore taken as the era cell. 8.11.4 (2018-08-15) is the final release of that line and the release the `node:8.11` tag resolved to at the January 2019 pin. No modern Node was substituted and no fallback was needed.
eraCell.evidenceQuality: a build-image fact, not a declared engines range — recorded as such, exactly as u3 stated it
eraCell.sha256Source: https://nodejs.org/dist/v8.11.4/SHASUMS256.txt — the published line and the measured digest of the downloaded bytes agree
eraCell.hostFact: the host is arm64 macOS 26.5.1 (Darwin 25.5.0). There is no darwin-arm64 build of Node 8 — the line predates Apple silicon support — so the darwin-x64 binary executes through Rosetta 2 translation, which is present and active on this host (oahd running). Inside the cell process.version/platform/arch report v8.11.4/darwin/x64, and that x64 identity is what made node-sass resolve a darwin-x64 prebuilt binding below.

nativeDependencies.node-sass@4.9.3: OBTAINED. Its installer downloaded the published prebuilt binding for this exact cell — https://github.com/sass/node-sass/releases/download/v4.9.3/darwin-x64-57_binding.node — saved to node_modules/node-sass/vendor/darwin-x64-57/binding.node and cached in the lane npm cache. No source build and no Python 2 dependency was hit. The darwin-x64/ABI-57 selection is a direct consequence of the Rosetta host fact above. node-sass is required by the build: angular.json's styles entry is Client/globals.scss.

laneSourceIntegrity.method: recursive diff of the work lane against the read-only corpus subpath, excluding node_modules and the build output directory
laneSourceIntegrity.duringInstall: npm 5.6.0 rewrote package-lock.json in place. 3866 lines changed across 5246 diff lines, and every one of them is a `"name": "spec"` pair inside a `requires` block, rewritten from the authored semver range to the already-resolved version (for example `"rxjs": "^6.0.0"` became `"rxjs": "6.2.2"`). Zero `version`, `resolved`, `integrity`, `dev`, `optional` or `bundled` lines differ, so the installed closure is exactly the closure the authored lock pins; the rewrite is a npm 5 lockfile-serialisation difference, not a resolution difference.
laneSourceIntegrity.rewriteArtefact: baseline/package-lock-npm-rewrite.diff — the complete diff, kept rather than summarised
laneSourceIntegrity.restoreProof: the authored lock was copied back from the read-only corpus after the install and before either build, so both production builds ran against a lane whose every authored file is byte-identical to the corpus. node_modules was not re-resolved after the restore.

postRestoreDiff.conclusion: every one of the 131 authored files in the work lane is byte-identical to the corpus; the lane holds node_modules and build output only

boundaries: This block establishes an era baseline only: the pinned WebSPA subpath installs and builds for production in its own Node 8.11 / Angular CLI 6.1.5 toolchain, and that build is byte-reproducible. Nothing else.
No migration, no adapter run, no witness journey and no browser observation happened in this unit, and none is claimed.
GREEN here says nothing about whether the frozen adapter carries the @angular/http surface this application still uses at six import sites. That is the stage-4 measurement.

The baseline was produced under Rosetta 2 translation on arm64 macOS. The bytes are reproducible on this host across runs; no claim is made that they are identical to bytes a native x64 or Linux node:8.11 container would produce.
The npm 5.6.0 lockfile rewrite is a finding about npm's serialisation, not evidence that the resolved closure drifted — the diff shows no version, resolved or integrity change.
This record establishes acquisition and read-only detection facts, nothing else.
The overturn of the gate-zero verdict is the Judge's, recorded in the T022 follow-up ruling and appended to the selection note; this unit did not re-decide it.
A RED at stage 4 is valid falsification of the frozen adapter and halts the run rather than reopening the freeze.
